title: Design Search Autocomplete
subtitle: Real-time typeahead suggestions using Trie data structures and pre-computed Top-K caches

stages.title: Stage 1 — SQL LIKE Query Search
stages.bottleneck: Executing SQL `SELECT * FROM queries WHERE text LIKE 'macb%'` on every single keystroke destroys DB performance.
stages.narrative:
**Naive Autocomplete.** Every keystroke fires an HTTP request that translates into a string prefix lookup in SQL.

**Failure mode:** At 50,000 queries/sec, the relational database experiences full table scans.

stages.title: Stage 2 — In-Memory Trie Data Structure
stages.bottleneck: Traversing deep Trie branches and sorting top 5 items dynamically at runtime is too expensive (`O(p + n + n log k)`).
stages.narrative: **Trie (Prefix Tree) Datastructure.** Store search query histories in a Trie tree where each node represents a character. Finding prefix matches takes `O(p)` where `p` is length of query string.

stages.title: Stage 3 — Pre-computed Top-5 at Each Trie Node + Redis Cache
stages.bottleneck: Updating frequency counts in real-time on live search traffic locks the Trie datastructure.
stages.narrative:
**Optimized Trie with Pre-computed Top 5.**
1. **Pre-computation:** Every Trie node stores an array of its top 5 most popular completion strings. Time complexity drops to `O(1)`!
2. **Redis Cache:** Front prefix queries (e.g. `q=m`, `q=ma`) are cached directly in Redis with a 1-hour TTL.

stages.title: Stage 4 — Offline Analytics Pipeline & Async Trie Builder
stages.bottleneck: Filtering objectionable content or trending news spikes safely.
stages.narrative: **Offline Pipeline & Real-Time Sync.** Search logs are aggregated asynchronously using Spark. A fresh snapshot of the Trie is built offline once a week (or hourly for trending topics) and hot-swapped into memory without downtime.
